messages:
incident-bot: ALERT -> synthetic check 'api-ingest-eu' breaching threshold (5 fails / 2m). paging on-call group: #oncall-inference. check: https://console.redwood.ai/synthetics/checked/api-ingest-eu :rotating_light:

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PDR-93421 triggered for service=synthetic-canary, urgency=high. Auto-escalation in 5m.

Maya: acked. I'm the on-call for inference, grabbing it. 

Jonas: saw the page. are we seeing customer impact or just probe flapping?

Maya: initial metrics — probe failures correlate with 5xx responses from router-v2 in eu-west-1 between 13:02-13:06 UTC. User-facing error rate up ~0.8% for a subset of routed traffic. Not widespread yet.

Priya: link to quick dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/infer/synth-eu?from=now-10m . latency percentiles also spiking for short bursts.

Sergio: any recent deploys or config changes to canary buckets?

Maya: no deploys in last 30m on runtime; there was a scheduled config rollout for synthetic probes at 12:50 to increase concurrency from 2->6 (PR #4821). rolling that back as a first mitigation.

Maya: running rollback: ```
# revert synth concurrency
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS" \
  https://ops.redwood.ai/api/v1/synthetics/rollout/4821/rollback
```

incident-bot: Note: rollback request accepted, rollout ID 4821 -> rollback started.

Jonas: good. also toggle the eu probe fanout to single-host while we investigate? that should reduce load and stop noisy failures.

Maya: doing that now: `opsctl synth set-config api-ingest-eu --fanout=1`

Priya: adding a temporary purple traffic tag to divert non-prod probes to a smaller pool: `synth-router apply --tag purple --target=pool-synth-small`

Sergio: checking infra: router-v2 logs show repeated downstream connection resets from a single autoscale instance (i-0a1b2c3d) in eu-west-1. It got put into rotation at 12:48 when scale event completed.

Maya: taking that instance OOS: `kubesvc drain i-0a1b2c3d && asg detach-instance i-0a1b2c3d`

Jonas: nice. if instance was unhealthy, that explains the 5xx bursts. can we mark the synthetic check as noise while we finish OOS? I want to avoid extra pages.

Maya: setting synth escalation to mute for 30m: `opsctl synth mute api-ingest-eu --duration=30m --reason "ongoing mitigation"` — done.

pagerduty: Incident PDR-93421 acknowledged by Maya.

Priya: customer impact note for incident timeline: "Between 13:02-13:06 UTC a subset of EU routed inference requests experienced elevated 5xxs (~0.8%) and latency spikes; root cause appears to be a recently scaled instance returning connection resets. Mitigation: drained and detached instance, rolled back synthetic concurrency rollout, reduced probe fanout. No broad customer errors observed; continuing monitoring."

Maya: will follow up with post-incident task to add a pre-rotation health-check gate to ASG scale-in/out and to add probe throttling limits.

Sergio: logs snippet for reference: ```
[13:03:12] router-v2[i-0a1b2c3d] ERROR downstream reset payload=conn_reset by peer
[13:03:15] router-v2[i-0a1b2c3d] 502 POST /v1/generate  - 120ms
[13:04:01] router-v2[i-0a1b2c3d] ERROR downstream reset payload=conn_reset by peer
```

Jonas: should we page infra on the unhealthy instance? might be a host-level networking issue.

Maya: already notifying infra: @pagerduty infra-team has been notified via the incident.

Priya: I'm updating the incident ticket with timeline and mitigation steps. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PDR-93421

Maya: monitoring dashboards — looks stable after drain and rollback. probe failures dropped to 0 in last 3m, user 5xx rate back to baseline.

Sergio: :thumbsup: nice quick ops.

Maya: leaving the synth muted for 30m, will hand off to Jonas for the next 30m in case anything flares. Jonas, can you take on-call next?

Jonas: yep taking over. I'll keep watch and follow up with infra on the instance root cause.

incident-bot: Incident PDR-93421 status -> acknowledged. current severity: high -> monitoring.

Maya: closing this thread for now; will update ticket with RCA draft in a few hours. thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
